info.title: Launchpoint Public API
info.description:
**Private preview.** The Launchpoint Public API is in private preview and available only to trusted partners we work with directly. Access is not self-serve. Email hi@launchpointhq.com to ask about access.

REST API for Launchpoint brands and agencies. Use an API key in the `x-api-key` header to authenticate.

## Requirements
- Public API access must be enabled for the company. During private preview, access is limited to trusted partners.
- Create and manage API keys in Dashboard → Settings → Developer.

## Creator privacy
- Responses never include creator email addresses. Creator phone numbers are null when no number is stored or the workspace does not have access to creator contact details.

## Rate limits
- Default: **100 requests per minute** per API key.
- Approved partner accounts: **400 requests per minute**.
- Every response includes `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset`. Requests over the limit return `429`.

## Errors
- Errors use `{ "error": "<message>" }` with the matching HTTP status. Some endpoints also include a `code`.

## Timestamps
- Timestamps are Unix timestamps in milliseconds unless a field says otherwise.

## Pagination
- Most list endpoints accept `page` and `limit` and return `{ data, page, total }`. Some also return `totalPages`.
- `scope=company` is the default. A parent agency key can pass `scope=agency` on supported routes to include its own data and linked brands.

get.description:
List public creator opportunities across Launchpoint for a jobs board or creator app. This catalog is platform-wide, not limited to the API key company. It includes only public, active campaigns that accept submissions and have not been deleted. Private, unlisted, paused, closed, and deleted deals are excluded.

Use each item’s `url` for the details action. It opens a public landing page before signup, with app, iPhone download, and web links. After installation or signup, a new creator must return to that page and open the deal again; automatic return through app installation is not supported.

This is not a personalized eligibility or pay feed. Launchpoint checks eligibility and shows current terms when the creator applies. The feed does not return creator identities, private budgets, or sourcing rewards.

The only query parameters are `page` and `limit`. Unsupported parameters, including `scope` and creator filters, return `400`. Results are ordered by stable deal ID. Fetch successive pages through `totalPages` to read the full catalog. Paging reads live state, so changes during a crawl can move rows between pages. Deduplicate by `id` and replace your cached catalog after each complete refresh.

200.description: Creator deals returned successfully. An empty catalog has data: [], total: 0, and totalPages: 0.

get.description:
Get the pay terms for each visible creator and program.

This endpoint includes offer-level cash terms and active Canvas payscales. `baseRateCents` contains cash entries only. Manual and Shopify entries are returned separately in `nonCashBaseRateEntries` with their `valueCents`; a product seed is not cash. `platformRatios: null` means there is no platform split. In the Canvas `assigned` block, `assignment: "explicit"` means the creator really resolves to that payscale group. `assignment: "campaign_default"` covers both a creator who was never assigned and a creator whose assigned group no longer exists; `assignedAt` is epoch milliseconds for an explicit assignment and is null for `campaign_default`.

parameters.name: creatorId
parameters.description: Narrow results to one opaque creator ID

payModelKind.description: The offer pricing kind, or `canvas_payscale` for a creator on Canvas

baseRateCents.description: Cash base-rate entries only, in the smallest currency unit

valueCents.description: Declared non-cash value; not included in baseRateCents

platformRatios.description: Platform split ratios. Null means no split.

assignment.description: `explicit` means the creator resolves to this payscale group. `campaign_default` means the creator was never assigned to a group or the assigned group no longer exists.

assignedAt.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds for an explicit assignment; null when `assignment` is `campaign_default`.

fallbackPay.description: The pay config used when content matches no rule. This can be null for a non-default payscale group with no fallback configured; null means the creator has no fallback pay yet.

400.description: Invalid creator ID or query parameter

403.description: The requested scope is not allowed

get.description:
Get saved audience demographics for each linked social account of a visible creator.

Percentages use a `0` to `100` scale, including `usAudiencePercentage`. Audience data can be up to about 30 days old; `lastUpdatedAt` is a Unix timestamp in milliseconds for the newest data in that account block. `countries` comes from the monthly country refresh when available and falls back to the Instagram account's own country split otherwise. `usAudiencePercentage` is populated only from the monthly country refresh, so null does not mean the US share is zero. A saved no-data marker can return `0`; that does not prove the US share is zero. `reason` is set only when the entire audience block has no data. When country data is missing but age, gender, or city data exists, `countriesReason` describes the missing country data instead.

The `instagramAudiences` entries expose separate populations Meta reports: people reached, people who engaged, and followers. These are different sets of people, so do not add them together.

The possible no-data reasons are `unsupported_platform`, `no_data_marker`, and `never_fetched`. A creator the API key cannot see returns `404`.

400.description: Creator ID is invalid

403.description: The requested scope is not allowed

404.description: Creator was not found or is not visible to this API key

get.description:
Get your company's programs with pagination and filters.

Programs are campaigns or marketing initiatives that creators take part in.

Get social media posts with detailed filters.

Filter posts by program, platform, creator, date range, and more. Each row includes direct links, thumbnails, stable creator IDs, cross-post group IDs, current metrics, metric availability, and the current UTC day's view change.

Platform copies of one source video remain separate rows because their links and metrics differ. Copies share `crossPostGroupId` so callers can group or de-duplicate them.

Agency accounts can pass `scope=agency` to return posts from the parent agency and every subaccount in one request.

parameters.description: Narrow results by program IDs (multiple allowed)

parameters.name: creator
parameters.description: Narrow results by creator IDs (multiple allowed)

crossPostGroupId.description: Shared by platform copies of the same source video

url.description: Direct URL for this platform post; an empty string means no URL is stored

deltaFromPrevDay.description: Signed change from the last snapshot before the current UTC day. A lower latest count produces a negative value. This is zero when no new snapshot was recorded today or when no earlier snapshot exists; the first stored total is a baseline, not views proven to have arrived today.

get.description:
Get full details for one post/video.

The response includes metrics, engagement data, payment status, and related contract/program information.


`description` is the post's caption. For an Instagram post on an account connected to Launchpoint, each metrics read replaces it with the current caption, so an edit by the creator appears after the next read. `descriptionFetchedAt` is the time of the read that returned it.

`account` is the social account that published the post.

descriptionFetchedAt.description: When the caption in `description` was read from the platform, in Unix milliseconds. Null when no read has stored it yet.

mediaUrl.description: Link that downloads the post's video or image file. Null unless media links are turned on for your workspace (email hi@launchpointhq.com). The link does not expire; do not share it. Also null when Launchpoint has no stored copy of the file.

account.description: The social account that published the post

profileFetchedAt.description: When the account's profile, including `bio` and `avatarUrl`, was last read from the platform, in Unix milliseconds

lastSyncedAt.description: When the post's metrics were last read. This is not the caption read time; see `descriptionFetchedAt`.

contract.description: Contract details, or null if the post creator has no offer-level contract.

get.description:
Get the latest stored Instagram performance and Reel watch metrics for one post.

`insights.status` and `insights.reason` are paired: `available` with `reason: null` means a post snapshot exists; `no_data` with `reason: never_fetched` means no post snapshot exists; and `no_data` with `reason: unsupported_platform` means the post is not Instagram.

`creatorAudience` is account-level audience data for the account that published the post. Its handle follows the same PII lock as the creator audience endpoint. It is not the geography of people who watched this video: Meta does not expose per-post country data at any access level. Instagram audience entries describe separate populations reported by Meta and should not be added together. Non-Instagram posts return `no_data` with `reason: unsupported_platform` instead of invented metrics.

updatedAt.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds for the stored post snapshot

400.description: Post ID is invalid

get.description:
Get the media analysis for one post: the storyboard scenes the analyzer wrote plus retention data.

`analysisStatus` is the state of the post's latest non-fingerprint analysis: `none` when the post has never been analyzed, `pending`, `failed`, or `complete`. `storyboard` is `null` until a complete analysis with scenes exists.

`retention.organic` follows the post insights contract: `status` and `reason` are paired — `available` with `reason: null` means an Instagram snapshot exists; `no_data` with `never_fetched` means none was stored; `no_data` with `unsupported_platform` means the post is not Instagram.

`retention.paid` sums the post's video paid metrics across all of its boosts: `impressions`, three-second views, and watch-through quartile counters (`videoP25Views` … `videoP100Views`), plus `hookRatePct` (three-second views ÷ impressions) and `completionRatePct` (completes ÷ impressions), both as percentages from 0 to 100. Paid metrics are video-level, so every crossposted sibling post of one video reports the same paid block. `no_data` with reason `no_paid_metrics` means the video has no reported paid metrics.

analyzedAt.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds of the latest analysis update

sellsProduct.description: Present on newer analyses; null on older artifacts

hookRatePct.description: Share still watching at 3s, percentage from 0 to 100 (1 − reels skip rate)

updatedAt.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds for the stored post snapshot

daysLive.description: Distinct days with a reported paid row

videoP25Views.description: Views that reached 25% of the video

videoP50Views.description: Views that reached 50% of the video

videoP75Views.description: Views that reached 75% of the video

videoP100Views.description: Views that reached 100% of the video

hookRatePct.description: Three-second views ÷ impressions, percentage from 0 to 100

storyboard.description: A person reacts in surprise to the product on a kitchen counter.

post.description:
Exclude a post in a canvas program from creator earnings. This is permanent. The exclusion covers the post's whole video, including its cross-posts on other platforms (same `crossPostGroupId`). The video stops counting in pay and analytics, its pending pay is removed, and it is not tracked again. Afterwards the posts are no longer returned by `/posts`.

With a `message`, the creator is told that the video will not be paid, and why. Without one, the creator is not told.

The request is refused with `409` and a `code` when real pay already reached the creator or a paid ad uses the video. `paid: false` in `/posts` does not guarantee that the exclusion is allowed.

reason.description: Earlier name for `message`. Send one of the two, not both.

creatorNotified.description: True when a reason was sent to the creator

400.description: Invalid post id or message, both `message` and `reason` sent, or the post is not in a canvas program

403.description: The program is read-only for this API key

404.description: Post not found or already excluded

409.description: Refused to protect money already paid. `code` is one of `already_paid`, `payout_processing`, `paid_off_platform`, `has_paid_ads`, `has_platform_fee`, `manual_payout_in_progress`, `removal_in_progress`.

get.description:
Get key performance indicators grouped by status.

The response includes:
- Programs (by status: active, draft, paused, etc.)
- Contracts (by status: active, pending, completed, etc.)
- Posts (total, views, engagement, paid/unpaid)
- Creators (total, with active contracts)

Agency accounts can pass `scope=agency` to calculate KPIs across the
parent agency and every subaccount.

Return an all-time creator leaderboard and program totals without paging through every post.

Provide the program ID in `program`. Every creator in the program is returned in descending order by current total views. Creator sub-profiles are folded into one client-stable root creator ID.

`totalPosts` counts platform post rows, so cross-posted copies count separately. `totalSourceVideos` counts distinct source videos and can be used for de-duplicated totals.

The normal analytics read model refreshes at :10 and :40 each hour, so its totals can trail a new metric scrape by about 30 minutes. Posts outside that read model fall back to their latest stored metric snapshot.

Agency accounts can pass `scope=agency` to access a program owned by the parent agency or one of its linked brands.

totalPosts.description: Number of platform post rows; cross-posted copies count separately

totalSourceVideos.description: Number of distinct source videos after grouping cross-posted copies

topCreators.description: Every program creator in descending order by total views

totalPosts.description: Number of platform post rows for this creator

totalSourceVideos.description: Number of distinct source videos for this creator

get.description:
Get analytics with filtering support.

Like the /overall page in the web app, this endpoint returns:
- Summary metrics
- Top performing posts
- Top performing creators
- Platform breakdown

When `fromDate` and/or `toDate` are provided, `summary` follows the same
activity attribution model as the dashboard Performance Overview chart:
- daily deltas from post `daily` stats
- first-stat totals attributed back to the upload date
- posts without daily stats attributed to their upload date

`snapshotSummary`, `topPosts`, `topCreators`, and `platformBreakdown`
stay as upload-date snapshot views, matching the `/overall` page tables.

Agency accounts can pass `scope=agency` to calculate the overview across
the parent agency and every subaccount.

get.description:
Comment-to-DM attribution for each visible program: how many leads opted in, how many got the first DM, and how many tapped the DM link.

Every row has the same fields. A field the chosen grouping does not use is `null`. Group the report with `groupBy`:

- `program` (default): one row per program.
- `account`: one row per program and creator account that sent the DMs.
- `post`: one row per program, creator account, and the post the lead commented on. `postId` is the id used by `GET /posts` when the post is tracked; otherwise it is `null`. A lead who DMed the keyword directly has no post, so that row has a `null` `platformPostId`.
- `day`: one row per day.

Each event counts on its own day in America/New_York, the same rule as the dashboard DMs sent and DM clicks tiles: an opt-in on the day the conversation opened, a DM on the day it was sent, a tap on the day of the tap. `fromDate` and `toDate` apply to those days, so a tap can fall in a range that does not include its DM.

Taps on links sent by Launchpoint's earlier comment automations (before 2026-09-27) are included and belong to their post. Opt-ins and sends from that period were not stored.

Sort with `sortBy` and `sortOrder` (default `desc`). `sortBy` defaults to `date` for `groupBy=day` and to `linkClicks` otherwise; `sortBy=date` works only with `groupBy=day`. Ties keep a stable order, so pages do not shift between reads. `summary` sums every row in the report, not only the current page.

parameters.description: Narrow the report to one program

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: Field to sort rows by. Defaults to `date` for groupBy=day and `linkClicks` otherwise. `date` needs groupBy=day

get.description:
Read-only summary of your company's payout wallet balances and lifetime activity.

These are the same metrics shown on the payouts dashboard:
- **Available balance** — funds ready to pay creators
- **Pending balance** — incoming top-ups still processing
- **Total owed** — calculated amount owed across active contracts
- **Lifetime deposits** — total confirmed wallet top-ups

All amounts are in USD dollars.

get.description:
Creator money for each visible program, using the same definition as the campaign pages in the dashboard.

`spend` is money sent to creators through Launchpoint (`paid`), money the brand paid creators directly (`paidOffPlatform`), and money still held for creators (`awaiting` is past its pay date, `tracking` is still inside its view window). Every field is returned in dollars and in cents.

This is different from `GET /payouts`, which lists money that left your own wallet. For an agency, a linked brand's wallet can fund the same creators, so summing the wallet ledger by program understates what creators earned. Use this endpoint for per-program spend reports.

`fromDate` and `toDate` pick posts by their publish day, the same rule as the dashboard date picker, not the day money moved. Rows are sorted by spend, and `summary` sums every program in the report, not only the current page.

get.description:
Get creators associated with your company, along with a contract status map for each campaign.
Use this to see which creators are active across your campaigns. Each creator has a
`phone` number, which is `null` when no number is on file or while your creator access is locked.
Creator email addresses are never returned.

The `campaigns` array lists every program a creator is or was contracted under,
along with its contract status. A creator's top-level `status` is `"active"` when they
have at least one active contract; otherwise, it is `"inactive"`.

Each campaign lists `enhancementOptIns`: the creator's accounts opted into that
program's enhancements, trial reels (`trialReels`) or comment-to-DM (`commentDm`).
A brand turns an enhancement on for a program; the creator then opts in per account.
An account opted into both has two entries. An opt-out removes the entry.

Ghost-handle contracts are excluded.

get.description:
Get creator applications to your Canvas programs, with each application's approval status.

An application is a creator's current enrollment in a Canvas program together with the campaign-level approval decision. `status` is `pending` while the application waits for review, `approved` once the creator is accepted, and `rejected` when the creator is turned down. A creator who joined before approvals existed is returned as `approved` with `decidedAt: null`.

Brief-based programs approve creators per brief and are not listed here.
